_what_this_is: The fixed taxonomy for Data/classify_topics.py. This file is the single source of truth for the category list; no discipline name is hardcoded in the Python.

source.title: Understanding Health-Related Discussions on Reddit: Development of a Topic Assignment Method and Exploratory Analysis
source.authors: Chan GJ, Fung M, Warrington J, Nowak SA
source._note: The paper sorts 82 fine-grained topics into 17 broader medical disciplines, grouped on the chapter codes of the ICD-10. We use the 17 disciplines: the 82 topics are too sparse at n=6,600 (see topic_classification_plan.md).

_provenance: All 17 names transcribed verbatim from Table 2 of the PDF, in the paper's own descending-frequency order. The relative frequencies are the paper's, measured on its own 78,890-post general-Reddit corpus, and are recorded here only as a prior: they are NOT r/AskDocs rates and should not be used as expected prevalences for our sample.
_other_label_note: Deliberately null. The published taxonomy already carries its own two escape hatches -- 'Medical; other' for a medical post fitting none of the rest, and 'Nonmedical' for a post with no medical subject -- so appending a third 'Other' would give the model overlapping categories to choose between and split the residue across them.
_fallback_label_note: Where an off-list label is coerced to when the model returns something outside the closed list. Counted as off_list and reported, never silent.
residual_guidance: Use "Medical; other" for a post with a genuine medical subject that fits none of the other categories. Use "Nonmedical" for a post with no medical subject at all, such as a question about the subreddit itself.
_residual_guidance_note: Rendered verbatim into the discipline prompt. The wording for the residual categories lives here with the category list rather than in the Python, so swapping the taxonomy swaps its guidance too.
category_rules: NEOPLASMS. ICD-10 Chapter II (C00-D49) covers benign neoplasms as well as malignant ones, so both are coded "Neoplasms", whichever organ is involved. A malignancy counts when it has been diagnosed, or when a clinician or a test has actually raised it (a biopsy, an imaging finding, an abnormal result, a referral); a poster's own worry about cancer is NOT enough, so a question about whether something might be cancer, about screening, or about family-history risk is coded to the organ system. A benign neoplasm counts when it is named as one: a benign tumour, lipoma, fibroid, adenoma or haemangioma. Lesions that are not neoplasms stay with the organ system - a cyst (ovarian cyst is N83, not Chapter II), an undifferentiated lump, a swollen lymph node, or a polyp not described as adenomatous (an unspecified colon polyp is K63.5). Code the organ system also when the post's primary concern is a non-neoplastic problem that happens to co-occur with a neoplasm or a cancer history.

CARE-PROCESS QUESTIONS. When the question is about the process of care -- whether it is rude to ask a doctor something, a delayed portal reply, how to communicate with a clinician, whether a discharge was appropriate -- but the post describes a specific complaint, code the complaint's discipline. "Nonmedical" is only for a post with no medical content at all.

EXPOSURES AND POISONING. Chemical, drug and environmental exposures -- a caustic ingestion, carbon monoxide, a medication overdose, swallowing a contaminant -- are coded "Medical; other". ICD-10 places poisoning and external causes in their own chapters (XIX and XX), outside the body-system chapters this taxonomy is built from, and the taxonomy has no toxicology category.
_category_rules_note:
Boundary rules rendered into the discipline prompt as additional bullets, and applied by the human coders during adjudication. They live here so the model and the coders are held to one rubric: scoring the classifier against a rule it was never given would understate it.
History: the Neoplasms rule was adopted 2026-10-08 to follow the ICD-10 chapter convention the taxonomy is built on, narrowed the same day from 'suspected' to 'clinically raised' (cancer_relevant deliberately counts posts merely about the possibility of cancer, so the broader wording would have made Neoplasms a worry category), then extended to benign neoplasms once the hand-coded data turned up an explicitly benign brain tumour that the malignancy-only wording did not decide. The care-process and exposure rules were adopted from the adjudication of the 42 queued posts, where both patterns recurred.
_cancer_node_note: Used only by --cancer-scope oncology. Note that the ICD-10 'Neoplasms' chapter covers benign as well as malignant neoplasms, so this node is broader than cancer; the cancer task decides malignancy itself and by default (--cancer-scope all) does not read this field.
